question: access

request.from: a cloud container in a datacenter network, one IP
request.body: an MCP initialize request (jsonrpc 2.0, protocolVersion 2025-06-18, clientInfo public-agents-researcher 1.0), then a tools/list on the same session, Content-Type application/json, Accept application/json and text/event-stream

headers.access-control-allow-headers: Content-Type, MCP-Session-Id, MCP-Protocol-Version, Mcp-Method, Mcp-Name, X-Context7-API-Key, Context7-API-Key, X-API-Key, Authorization

decoded.challenge: www-authenticate: Bearer, resource_metadata="https://mcp.context7.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource", sent on the 200 (the comma after the scheme is the record's, not the header's: the schema's credential rule refuses the verbatim value; the transcript has it as sent)
decoded.initialize: 200, SSE; serverInfo Context7 4.1.1 with websiteUrl, description and an icon; protocolVersion 2025-06-18
decoded.tools-list: 200 with no session id issued: 2 tools (resolve-library-id, query-docs); the same challenge header rides on this 200 too
decoded.protected-resource-metadata: 200 at the origin-level URL the challenge names; resource https://mcp.context7.com; authorization_servers: https://clerk.context7.com and https://context7.com (two); scopes_supported profile, email; bearer_methods_supported header
decoded.authorization-server-metadata: 200 at https://clerk.context7.com/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server (the first server named; the second was not fetched); issuer clerk.context7.com; registration, authorization and token endpoints on clerk.context7.com; scopes openid, profile, email, public_metadata, private_metadata, offline_access; grants authorization_code, refresh_token, device_code; token auth client_secret_basic, none, client_secret_post; PKCE S256
decoded.rest: GET https://context7.com/api/v2/libs/search?query=astro with no Authorization header answers 200 with a JSON results list (the first result /withastro/docs)

finding: With no credentials, an MCP initialize POST to mcp.context7.com/mcp answers 200 (Context7 4.1.1) and a tools/list answers 200 with two tools, resolve-library-id and query-docs. Both 200s carry a www-authenticate header naming a protected-resource document, which is a challenge on a success: the server serves the keyless caller and tells it where to authenticate at the same time, and the CORS allow-list names four API-key header spellings beside Authorization. The resource document names two authorization servers, clerk.context7.com and context7.com, and lists two scopes; the Clerk server publishes registration, the device-code grant and public clients (none), with six scopes of its own. Which server an agent should use, and what a credential changes in the two tools, is not published here and not measured. A keyless GET on the documented library-search API answers 200. Same 200s as the 2026-09-08 measurement in the entry's notes; the challenge on the 200, the two-server resource document and the Clerk metadata are recorded here for the first time. Nothing here measures what either server does with a credential.
